# gradepack task registry

Static API: https://gatlavishweshwarreddy.github.io/gradepack/api/tasks/<id>.json

A collection of realistic Python debugging tasks with automated graders.
Each task has a starter file with a deliberate bug and a grader with pytest tests.

## Tasks

### 001-pagination-off-by-one
Title: Fix the off-by-one error in pagination
Difficulty: easy
Tags: pagination, off-by-one, arithmetic
Estimated minutes: 15
Prompt: The function paginate(items, page, per_page) in starter/paginate.py returns a slice of items for a 1-indexed page. It returns the wrong result on the last page when len(items) is not an exact multiple of per_page. Fix the total_pages calculation so that paginate(list(range(1,11)), 4, 3) == [10] and all other grader tests pass. Do not edit the tests.

### 002-csv-parse-strip
Title: Fix CSV header and value whitespace stripping
Difficulty: easy
Tags: parsing, strings, csv
Estimated minutes: 10
Prompt: The function parse_csv(text) in starter/parse_csv.py parses a CSV string and returns a list of dicts mapping header names to values. It has two bugs: (1) header names are not stripped of leading/trailing whitespace, and (2) row values are not stripped of leading/trailing whitespace. Fix both so that parse_csv(' name , age\nAlice , 30\n Bob,25') returns [{'name': 'Alice', 'age': '30'}, {'name': 'Bob', 'age': '25'}]. The function must handle an empty string by returning an empty list. Do not edit the tests.

### 003-date-diff
Title: Fix elapsed days calculation to ignore time component
Difficulty: medium
Tags: datetime, stdlib
Estimated minutes: 15
Prompt: The function days_between(d1, d2) in starter/date_diff.py accepts two ISO-8601 date strings (YYYY-MM-DD) and returns the absolute number of days between them as an integer. The current implementation includes an off-by-one error caused by using datetime instead of date, and it fails when dates are passed in reverse order. Fix it so that days_between('2024-01-01', '2024-01-10') == 9, days_between('2024-01-10', '2024-01-01') == 9 (absolute), days_between('2023-12-31', '2024-01-01') == 1, and days_between('2024-02-28', '2024-03-01') == 2. Do not edit the tests.

### 004-word-frequency
Title: Fix word frequency counter to normalise case and strip punctuation
Difficulty: easy
Tags: strings, parsing, normalization
Estimated minutes: 10
Prompt: The function word_frequency(text) in starter/word_frequency.py returns a dict mapping each word to its count. It has two bugs: (1) it is case-sensitive so 'Hello' and 'hello' are counted separately, and (2) it does not strip punctuation so 'word.' and 'word' are counted separately. Fix it so that word_frequency('Hello, hello! World.') returns {'hello': 2, 'world': 1}. Words are separated by whitespace. Punctuation means any character that is not a letter or digit. An empty string returns {}. Do not edit the tests.

### 005-lru-cache
Title: Fix LRU cache eviction order
Difficulty: medium
Tags: data-structures, caching, state
Estimated minutes: 20
Prompt: The class LRUCache in starter/lru_cache.py implements a fixed-capacity least-recently-used cache with get(key) and put(key, value) methods. get returns the value or -1 if the key is not present, and accessing a key via get counts as a use. put inserts or updates; if the cache is at capacity the least-recently-used key must be evicted first. The bug is that get does not update the recency of the accessed key, so the eviction order is wrong. Fix get so that it moves the accessed key to the most-recently-used position. Do not edit the tests.

### 006-stack-with-min
Title: Fix constant-time minimum tracking in a stack
Difficulty: medium
Tags: data-structures, state, stack
Estimated minutes: 20
Prompt: The class MinStack in starter/min_stack.py supports push(val), pop(), and get_min() all in O(1) time. The bug is in pop(): it always pops from the min-stack, even when the popped value is not the current minimum, so get_min() returns wrong values after pops. Fix pop() so that it only removes from the min-stack when the value being popped equals the current minimum. Do not edit the tests.

### 007-slug-generator
Title: Fix URL slug generator
Difficulty: easy
Tags: strings, regex, normalization
Estimated minutes: 10
Prompt: The function slugify(text) in starter/slugify.py converts a string to a URL slug: lowercase, words joined by hyphens, all characters that are not letters or digits replaced by hyphens, consecutive hyphens collapsed to one, and leading/trailing hyphens removed. The starter has three bugs: (1) it does not lowercase the result, (2) it does not collapse consecutive hyphens, and (3) it does not strip leading/trailing hyphens. Fix all three. Examples: slugify('Hello World') == 'hello-world', slugify('  Hello   World  ') == 'hello-world', slugify('Hello, World!') == 'hello-world', slugify('Python 3.11') == 'python-3-11'. Do not edit the tests.

### 008-run-length-encoding
Title: Fix run-length encoding to merge consecutive identical characters
Difficulty: easy
Tags: encoding, strings, off-by-one
Estimated minutes: 15
Prompt: The function encode(s) in starter/rle.py returns a run-length encoded list of (char, count) tuples. The bug is that it starts a new run for every character instead of incrementing the count for a run of identical characters. Fix it so that encode('aaabbc') == [('a', 3), ('b', 2), ('c', 1)] and encode('') == []. Also fix decode(pairs) which reconstructs the original string from a list of (char, count) tuples — it currently has an off-by-one and repeats each character count-1 times instead of count times. Do not edit the tests.

### 009-token-bucket
Title: Fix token bucket rate limiter refill logic
Difficulty: hard
Tags: rate-limiting, state, arithmetic
Estimated minutes: 25
Prompt: The class TokenBucket in starter/token_bucket.py implements a token-bucket rate limiter. __init__(rate, capacity) sets the fill rate (tokens per second) and the maximum capacity. consume(n, now) attempts to consume n tokens at time `now` (a float, seconds). It must first refill tokens based on elapsed time since the last call (tokens = rate * elapsed, capped at capacity), then consume n tokens if available and return True, or return False without consuming if insufficient. The starter has two bugs: (1) it adds tokens without capping at capacity, and (2) it does not update self._last after a failed consume, so time keeps accumulating wrongly. Fix both. Do not edit the tests.

### 010-json-flattener
Title: Fix nested JSON flattener key path construction
Difficulty: medium
Tags: data-transformation, recursion, dicts
Estimated minutes: 20
Prompt: The function flatten(obj, sep='.') in starter/flatten.py flattens a nested dict into a single-level dict with dot-separated keys. The bug is that when recursing, it prepends the separator even for top-level keys, producing keys like '.a.b' instead of 'a.b'. Fix it so that flatten({'a': {'b': 1, 'c': 2}, 'd': 3}) == {'a.b': 1, 'a.c': 2, 'd': 3}. An empty dict returns {}. Lists are treated as leaf values and not recursed into. Do not edit the tests.

### 011-iso-week
Title: Fix ISO week number calculation at year boundaries
Difficulty: medium
Tags: datetime, stdlib, calendar
Estimated minutes: 20
Prompt: The function iso_week(date_str) in starter/iso_week.py accepts an ISO date string (YYYY-MM-DD) and returns a tuple (iso_year, week_number) using the ISO 8601 definition. The starter uses the wrong strftime directives: it uses %Y (calendar year) instead of %G (ISO year) and %W (Monday-based week, 0-indexed) instead of %V (ISO week number). This causes wrong results at year boundaries. Fix it so that iso_week('2024-12-30') == (2025, 1), iso_week('2025-01-01') == (2025, 1), iso_week('2023-01-01') == (2022, 52). Do not edit the tests.

### 012-retry-decorator
Title: Fix retry decorator to catch only the specified exception types
Difficulty: medium
Tags: decorators, exceptions, state
Estimated minutes: 20
Prompt: The function retry(max_attempts, exceptions) in starter/retry.py is a decorator factory. It wraps a function so that if it raises one of the listed exception types it is retried up to max_attempts times total (not max_attempts extra times). After exhausting all attempts, the last exception is re-raised. The starter has two bugs: (1) it catches all BaseException instead of only the specified exception types, so unrelated exceptions are silently retried; and (2) the attempt counter starts at 0 but the loop condition is wrong, allowing max_attempts+1 total calls instead of max_attempts. Fix both. Do not edit the tests.

### 013-timezone-scheduler
Title: Event scheduler returns wrong times in non-UTC zones
Difficulty: medium
Tags: datetime, timezone, scheduler
Estimated minutes: 20
Prompt: The module starter/scheduler.py provides EventScheduler. add_event(name, utc_dt) stores an event by name with its UTC time. next_event_in(tz_name) should return a (name, timedelta) tuple for the nearest upcoming event, where the timedelta is computed relative to the current time in the given timezone. The method relies on a clock helper in starter/clock.py that returns the current time. When tested against a non-UTC zone such as 'America/New_York' or 'Asia/Tokyo', next_event_in returns a timedelta whose magnitude is wrong — it differs from the correct value by several hours. All other tests (empty scheduler, past events, exact ties) must also pass. Do not edit the tests.

### 014-mutable-default
Title: Accumulator instances share state unexpectedly
Difficulty: easy
Tags: classes, state, python-gotcha
Estimated minutes: 10
Prompt: The module starter/accumulator.py defines an Accumulator class. Each Accumulator should maintain its own independent list of items, and the list should start empty for every new instance unless an initial list is explicitly provided to the constructor. When a second Accumulator is created and items are appended to it, the first Accumulator must not see those items and vice versa. The grader checks that two independently-constructed Accumulator instances have separate item lists and that appending to one does not affect the other. Do not edit the tests.

### 015-sliding-window-max
Title: Sliding window maximum produces incorrect results
Difficulty: medium
Tags: algorithms, deque, sliding-window
Estimated minutes: 20
Prompt: The function sliding_max(nums, k) in starter/window.py returns a list of the maximum value in each contiguous window of size k over nums. For an input of length n the result must have n-k+1 elements. The function gives incorrect maximums for certain inputs — in particular when the true maximum is in the right half of a window rather than the left. For example sliding_max([1,3,1,2], 3) should be [3,3] but returns a wrong value. The grader checks correctness against several reference cases including varied window sizes, duplicate values, and single-element windows. Do not edit the tests.

### 016-decimal-money
Title: Ledger balance is inaccurate for certain decimal amounts
Difficulty: easy
Tags: decimal, arithmetic, money
Estimated minutes: 10
Prompt: The module starter/ledger.py provides a Ledger class. add(amount_str) records a monetary amount supplied as a string such as '0.10' or '19.99'. balance() returns the running total rounded to two decimal places. For amounts that cannot be represented exactly in binary, balance() returns a value that differs from the arithmetically correct sum — for example three additions of '0.10' yield 0.30 but the ledger may return a slightly different value. The grader checks exact equality of the balance against the expected decimal sum for several sequences of additions including common problem values. Do not edit the tests.

### 017-unicode-dedup
Title: String deduplicator keeps visually identical duplicates
Difficulty: medium
Tags: unicode, normalization, strings
Estimated minutes: 15
Prompt: The function dedup(strings) in starter/dedup.py removes duplicate strings from a list, preserving first occurrence and original ordering, and returns the deduplicated list. When the input contains strings that look identical on screen but are encoded differently — for example a character written as a single precomposed code point versus the same character written as a base letter plus a combining mark — dedup treats them as distinct and keeps both. The grader checks that dedup collapses such visually identical pairs into a single entry, while still preserving order and removing exact byte-level duplicates. Do not edit the tests.

### 018-thread-safe-cache
Title: Memoize decorator returns stale or incorrect cached values
Difficulty: hard
Tags: caching, threading, decorators
Estimated minutes: 25
Prompt: The module starter/memo.py exports memoize(fn), a decorator that caches the return value of fn keyed on its arguments. Calling a memoized function twice with the same arguments should return the same value both times without calling fn again. The grader checks: (1) that calling the decorated function twice with equal argument tuples returns the same value and does not invoke the underlying function a second time; (2) that different argument tuples produce independently cached results; (3) that the cache is safe to use from multiple threads without corrupting results. The current implementation fails at least one of these checks. Do not edit the tests.

### 019-invoice-total
Title: Invoice total is wrong when both discount and tax apply
Difficulty: hard
Tags: arithmetic, ordering, money
Estimated minutes: 20
Prompt: The package in starter/ implements a simple invoicing module. invoice.py provides Invoice with add_line(description, unit_price, quantity), discount(rate) to set a percentage discount (0.0–1.0), and total(tax_rate) which returns the final amount after applying the discount and then tax. tax.py provides apply_tax(amount, rate). discount.py provides apply_discount(amount, rate). When both a discount and a tax are applied the returned total is wrong — it does not match the value computed by discounting the subtotal first and then applying tax to the discounted amount. The grader compares total() against a reference calculation for several combinations of line items, discount rates, and tax rates. Results must be rounded to two decimal places. Do not edit the tests.

### 020-log-parser
Title: Log parser reports wrong duration for entries spanning midnight
Difficulty: hard
Tags: datetime, parsing, edge-cases
Estimated minutes: 25
Prompt: The package in starter/ implements a log file parser. parser.py provides parse_log(lines) which parses lines of the form 'HH:MM:SS LEVEL message' and returns a list of LogEntry objects with fields: time (datetime.time), level (str), message (str). stats.py provides duration_seconds(entries) which returns the elapsed time in seconds between the first and last log entry. filter.py provides filter_level(entries, level) returning only entries at the given level. When a log spans midnight — the first entry is before 00:00:00 and the last is after — duration_seconds returns a negative or very small value instead of the correct positive elapsed time. The grader checks duration_seconds for log sequences that do and do not span midnight, and checks filter_level for correctness. Do not edit the tests.

### 021-config-merger
Title: Config merger mutates the base config when merging nested keys
Difficulty: hard
Tags: dict, deep-copy, merge
Estimated minutes: 20
Prompt: The package in starter/ implements a configuration merger. merger.py provides merge(base, override) which performs a deep merge: keys present only in base are kept, keys present only in override are added, and keys present in both are merged recursively if both values are dicts, otherwise the override value wins. loader.py provides load_config(path) which reads a JSON file and returns a dict. The bug: after merge(base, override) is called, the base dict (or its nested dicts) may be modified in place, so calling merge a second time with a different override produces wrong results. The grader calls merge twice with the same base and two different overrides and checks that both results are correct and that base is unchanged. Do not edit the tests.

### 022-permissions
Title: Permission checker grants access when it should deny
Difficulty: hard
Tags: rbac, identity, bugs
Estimated minutes: 20
Prompt: The package in starter/ implements a role-based access control checker. roles.py defines a Role dataclass with name (str) and permissions (frozenset of str). permissions.py provides has_permission(user_roles, permission) which returns True if any role in user_roles grants the given permission. A user may have multiple roles; the check should return True only when at least one role's permissions set contains the exact permission string. For certain permission strings the function incorrectly returns True when it should return False, or False when it should return True. The grader checks has_permission for users with zero, one, and multiple roles, with permissions present in some roles but not others, using several permission string values. Do not edit the tests.

### 023-inventory
Title: Inventory reservation allows overbooking under concurrent requests
Difficulty: hard
Tags: inventory, concurrency, state
Estimated minutes: 25
Prompt: The package in starter/ implements an inventory reservation service. inventory.py provides Inventory with add_stock(item, qty), available(item) returning current uncommitted quantity, and reserve(item, qty) which should atomically decrement the available stock and return True, or return False without changing stock if qty exceeds what is available. reservation.py provides ReservationLog that records committed reservations. The bug: reserve() reads available() and then writes, but the available() calculation does not account for reservations that are already committed, so multiple callers can each observe sufficient stock and all succeed, resulting in total reserved quantity exceeding actual stock. The grader checks that the sum of successful reservations never exceeds initial stock, using seeded sequences of concurrent-style reservation attempts. Do not edit the tests.

### 024-csv-importer
Title: CSV importer rejects valid numeric values in certain formats
Difficulty: hard
Tags: csv, coercion, parsing
Estimated minutes: 20
Prompt: The package in starter/ implements a CSV importer with schema validation. importer.py provides import_csv(rows, schema) where rows is a list of dicts (as from csv.DictReader) and schema is a dict mapping column names to type names ('int', 'float', 'str'). coerce.py provides coerce(value, type_name) which converts a string value to the target Python type. schema.py provides validate_schema(schema) which checks that all type names are valid. The bug: coerce() raises ValueError for integer columns when the CSV contains values like '1.0' or '2.0' — whole numbers formatted as floats — even though those values represent valid integers. The grader checks that import_csv correctly coerces '1.0', '42.0', and similar float-formatted integers to int, and raises ValueError only for genuinely non-numeric values. Do not edit the tests.

### 025-rate-limiter
Title: Rate limiter allows one extra request per window
Difficulty: hard
Tags: rate-limiting, sliding-window, off-by-one
Estimated minutes: 20
Prompt: The package in starter/ implements a sliding-window rate limiter. limiter.py provides RateLimiter(max_requests, window_seconds) with allow(key, now) which returns True if the given key has made fewer than max_requests requests in the window ending at now, and records the request if allowed. store.py provides RequestStore which manages per-key timestamps. The bug: when exactly max_requests have been made within the window, allow() returns True (permits one extra) instead of False. The grader checks that after exactly max_requests calls allow() returns False for the same key, that different keys have independent limits, and that requests older than window_seconds are correctly expired. Do not edit the tests.

### 026-retry-client
Title: HTTP client does not retry all transient errors and backoff is wrong
Difficulty: hard
Tags: http, retry, backoff
Estimated minutes: 25
Prompt: The package in starter/ implements an HTTP client with retry logic. client.py provides HttpClient(transport, max_retries, backoff_base) with get(url) which calls transport.request(url) and retries on transient failures. transport.py provides FakeTransport, a controllable test double that returns pre-configured responses. backoff.py provides wait_seconds(attempt, base) returning the backoff delay for a given attempt number. The client retries on some error status codes but not others that should also be retried, and the backoff delay for the second and subsequent retries is wrong — it does not grow exponentially from the base. The grader checks that the client retries on all required 5xx status codes, that the number of calls to transport matches expectations, and that wait_seconds returns the correct exponential series. Do not edit the tests.
